newsitem.title: UK: First Beatles-only auction to be held in Japan.
newsitem.headline: First Beatles-only auction to be held in Japan.

text.p: The first international auction devoted entirely to Beatles memorabilia will take place in Tokyo on March 22, British auctioneers Bonhams said Tuesday.
The auction, expected to fetch more than one million pounds ($1.6 million), will include a Hofner guitar once owned by Paul McCartney amd his hand-written lyrics for the song "Penny Lane."
Bonhams said the sale would be beamed to an expected 25 million households in Britain and other European countries via the new British-based Auction Channel cable television company.
"We thought we would hold the auction in Tokyo because of the enormous Beatle interest in Japan," said Bonham entertainment expert Ted Owen.
Television viewers will be able to make bids by telephone, fax or through the Internet to the auction room in Tokyo, which will have a satellite link with Bonhams' sale room in London.

McCartney's 1964 left-handed custom-made Hofner bass guitar, which was used by him in the 1960s, is expected to fetch up to 150,000 pounds ($249,000). The "Penny Lane" lyrics have an estimated price of 50,000 pounds ($83,000).
Other items include a tape recording of a radio interview with John Lennon and Yoko Ono in 1971, shortly after The Beatles split up.

McCartney, who was given a knighthood last month by Queen Elizabeth, hit out recently at memorabilia hunters and took legal action to stop a British woman selling a scrap of paper containing the lyrics of "With A Little Help From My Friends."
He got a court injunction against the private sale, saying the words of the song belonged jointly to The Beatles as a band.

"To show how ridiculous this whole memorabilia market has become, there is currently someone in the U.S.A. who owns my own birth certificate. How people can feel that that is right is beyond my comprehension," McCartney said.
